sentences.text: The petitioner faces allegations of having committed the offences under Sections 498A, 342, 323, 324, 326, 354(B), 506 II r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. The facts of the case are as follows: the 2 nd respondent, who is the defacto complainant in Crime no.99/2017, is the former wife of the petitioner's brother.
The 2nd respondent gave a First Information Statement on 17-01-2017 leading to registration of Crime No.99/2017, where there is absolutely no allegation against the petitioner herein.

The only allegation in the First Information Statement given on 17-01-2017 is the following:

sentences.text: Annexure-II is the copy of the petition filed by the 2 nd respondent for the same.
In Annexure-II also there is absolutely no allegation against the petitioner.
However, certain allegations were raised against the father-in-law and mother-in-law of the 2nd respondent.

The said allegation is as follows:
"4.      2  3   -- 2  3                                       
.
xxxx xxxx

xxxx" 
However, in a statement given on 18-01-2017 there was an allegation as follows:
" xxxx xxxx xxxx           
      
  .
xxxx xxxx xxxx"
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that none of the offences alleged against Rubeena vs State Of Kerala on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55747778/
2 the petitioner can be stated to have been committed by the petitioner.

It is submitted that in the First Information Statement leading to registration of Crime No.99/2017 and also in the petition given, seeking direction from the court regarding investigation, there is absolutely no whisper against the petitioner.

It is preposterous that the petitioner has been arrayed as a 4 th accused in C.C.No.1580/2021.
4.
Learned counsel for the 2nd respondent vehemently opposes the grant of any relief.
It is submitted that a reading of the final report will show that there are clear allegations against the petitioner as well.
It is submitted that merely because the name of the petitioner is not specifically mentioned in the First Information Statement that does not mean that there is no allegation against the petitioner.

It is submitted that the First Information Statement clearly states that relatives of the husband of the 2 nd respondent had also harassed her in the manner set out in the First Information Statement.
5. Heard the learned Senior Public Prosecutor also.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Senior Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel for the 2nd respondent, I am of the view that no allegation can be raised against the petitioner that she had committed the offences alleged against her in C.C.No.1580/2021.

The learned counsel for the petitioner is right in contending that, when there was no allegation whatsoever against the petitioner in the First Information Statement leading to registration of Crime No.99/2017 as also in the petition filed before the court seeking directions regarding the investigation, the petitioner could not have been arrayed as the 4th accused alleging commission of offences mentioned above.
A reading of the final report also does not suggest that the petitioner has committed any of the offences alleged against him.

Accordingly, this Crl.M.C. is allowed and all further proceedings in C.C.No1580/2021 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Mattanchery, Ernakulam district (arising out of Crime No.99/2017 of Fort Kochi Police Station, Ernakulam district), will stand quashed as against the petitioner.
